text:
Some personal thoughts on $NVDA and Jensen.

The cut feels rushed to me.

On Sunday, the board said it had confidence in him. By Thursday, he was gone, effective immediately. This is a founder who built the company over 30+ years and put it at the center of the entire AI build-out, and the exit came with no permanent successor, an investigation still open, and earnings days away.

I'm not defending the personal stuff. That's on him, and he owned it. But there's a difference between accountability and a decision made under a week of headline pressure. Boards usually move slower on something this big, especially when the facts are still coming in.

When things move this fast, I tend to think we haven't heard the full story yet, one way or another.

As a trader, my job isn't to pick a side in the drama. It's to watch how price handles it. But as someone who's watched what he built, it feels like a strange way for that chapter to end.

We'll see what 11/17 brings.

zh_summary: 大多數股票不會直線上漲。它們上漲、崩跌，然後再次上漲，如果故事仍然真實，下跌就是賺錢的地方。$PLTR在2021年初漲到45美元。然後跌到7-8美元，底部接近6美元。超過80%的回撤。所有人都放棄了它。業務卻持續建設。
text:
Most stocks do not go up in a straight line. They go up, they fall apart, and then they go up again — and the fall is where the money is made, if the story is still true.

$PLTR went to $45 in early 2021. Then it fell to $7-8, and the bottom printed near $6. More than an 80% drawdown. Everyone wrote it off. The business kept building — government contracts, then commercial, then AI — and the stock went to $207. Then it fell again, nearly 50%, to about $107. And then it went to $209.

That is the whole lesson. A 50-80% pullback is not always a broken stock. Sometimes it is the same stock, the same story, at a price that makes sense again. The market does not hand out second chances quietly — it hands them out while everyone is busy calling the name dead.

Revisit the names you liked at the top. Check if the story changed or only the price did. If the story is intact and the price is half of what it was, that is not a warning. That is the opportunity.

text:
I've seen a lot of commentary around $SE sales & marketing spend, but I think it's worth putting the numbers into context.

A few things stand out:

1. The relationship isn't always immediate. 
In Q3 2023, incremental S&M spend increased by $424m against $215m of incremental revenue. The following quarter, incremental revenue rose to $306m while incremental S&M spend fell to just $49m. There can clearly be a lag.

2. Look at the latest numbers. 
In Q2 2026, incremental revenue was $690m against $246m of incremental S&M. In Q3, that improved to $795m against $227m. That's $3.50 of incremental revenue for every additional dollar of S&M.

3. Monetisation and GMV growth aren't mutually exclusive. 
Higher take rates are positive, but sustainability depends on maintaining competitive seller economics and consumer value.

For me, the question isn't simply how much $SE is spending on S&M, but what return it's generating. The latest numbers suggest the investment is translating into meaningful revenue growth.

$NBIS Path for NBIS to $1,000 Is that possible ? 

NBIS is currently a stock that trades around $115 with a market cap ~$34B. To hit $1,000/share it needs a $280–300B market cap or 8-9× current.

How it could happen:

2026 revenue: ~$3.0–3.2B
2027 guidance: $12–13B (4×) with pre-tax break-even in Q4

Longer term: Successful ramp to multi-GW active capacity by ~2030 could drive revenue to $40 - 60B+ (supported by Microsoft/Meta contracts, >$20 - 25M per MW pricing, and >1 GW/year additions).

At $50B revenue and 5–6× sales, market cap reaches ~$250-300B or 850-1,050/share (assuming limited dilution).

Main supports: Strong customer prepayments funding most new capex, vertical integration, and high AI demand.

Like in any other business there are always some risks : Build delays, funding/dilution from $40B+ annual capex, competition, or demand slowdown.

$1,000 is a multi-year bull-case scenario, not a near-term target. 

Is that possible? Well, there are some folks on X with clearly deep knowledge in the biz calling for a $2,000+ bull scenario.

zh_summary: David Friedberg 推測 Jensen Huang 被「拿下」是因為他反對政府控制 AI。「我確實擔心新國會將有立法說每個 AI 芯片、每台電腦和每個數據中心都有開關並連接到某個中央系統。而那個中央系統將是國家系統。如果這類事情發生，我們基本上在看一個奧威爾式國家爆炸。我的猜測是人們知道 Jensen 的哲學。Jensen 談了很多關於 AI 為全人類的利益，無論你的國家、地位、財富。他反對寡頭。他是寡頭的反面。中央國家、極權國家代表我相信 Jensen 反對的一切。因此，我認為如果最終目標是讓極權國家使用這項技術作為工具，他必須被拿下。我真的擔心那是原因。因為最終，下一位必須與立法機構合作制定我們都同意的法案，點頭，站在國會前說『你知道嗎？我同意這些新想法。讓我們都去做。』突然美國政府控制了存在於自由市場和全球數據中心的實際物理芯片。那對我們任何人來說都不是好地方。」
text:
David Friedberg speculates Jensen Huang was 'taken out' because he opposed government control of AI

“I do worry that there is legislation coming our way with the new Congress that is going to say every AI chip and every computer and every data center has a switch and has a connection back to some central system. And that central system will be a state system. And we are fundamentally looking at an Orwellian state explosion if this sort of thing happens.

“And my guess is that people know Jensen’s philosophy. Jensen has talked a lot about AI being for the benefit of all of humanity, regardless of your country, regardless of your standing, regardless of your wealth. He was anti-oligopoly. He was the opposite of the oligarchy.

“And the central state, the totalitarian state, represents everything that I believe Jensen was against. And because of that, I think he had to be taken out if ultimately the goal is to have the totalitarian state use this technology as a tool. I really do worry about that being the reason.

“Because at the end of the day, whoever comes in next has to be cooperative with legislatures and work out a bill that we all agree to, head nodding, standing in front of Congress and saying, ‘You know what? I agree with these new ideas. Let’s all go do this.’

“And suddenly the US government has control of the actual physical chips that exist in free markets and exist in data centers around the world. And that’s not a great place for any of us.”

Oscar Health’s results indicate improving economics for well-positioned ACA insurers, not a uniformly improving healthcare environment. The most actionable distinction is between companies retaining more premium through repricing and those absorbing the financial consequences when patients lose coverage. Oscar’s $250 million favorable risk adjustment revision is company-specific and should not be extrapolated across competing insurers. The strongest positive external implications concern Centene’s marketplace recovery, Allstate’s directly identified supplemental-insurance distribution opportunity, and eHealth’s employer-funded individual coverage channel. The strongest negative implications concern hospital payer mix and the continuing cost of verifying and retaining eligible ACA enrollment. Several supporting peer disclosures preceded Oscar’s call; the incremental information is corroboration and improved visibility, not a newly announced earnings event.

name: Damnang
zh_summary: Cerebras不使用HBM，但據其自身計算，運行Kimi K3需要59片晶圓。簡單聲稱不需要HBM只是行銷話術。目前其角色是在某些推理工作負載中取代GPU，或與AMD互補，AMD GPU處理預填充與長上下文，而Cerebras處理解碼以快速生成回應。他們正朝向3D堆疊DRAM發展，最終也需競爭記憶體供應。在目前供應鏈限制下此方法或有意義，但必須克服晶圓級晶片的技術限制，並在模型與系統變大時證明能持續有效運作。
text:
They don’t use HBM, but… by their own calculations, running Kimi K3 requires 59 wafers. Leaving that part out and simply saying “we don’t need HBM” is just marketing wordplay.

For now, I see their role as replacing GPUs in certain inference workloads or complementing AMD. AMD GPUs handle prefill, processing the input and long context, while Cerebras handles decode, generating the response quickly.

They understand these limitations too, which is why they’re moving toward 3D stacked DRAM. Eventually, they’ll have to compete for memory supply as well.

Still, I personally think this approach could make sense given the supply chain constraints we’re facing right now. The biggest question is how far they can overcome the technical limitations of wafer scale chips. Whether they can keep operating efficiently as models and systems get larger is something they’ll have to keep proving.

text:
TWO MAJOR NVIDIA SHAREHOLDERS HAVE WRITTEN TO THE BOARD ASKING IT TO LEAVE THE DOOR OPEN FOR JENSEN HUANG'S RETURN

Brad Gerstner, chief executive of Altimeter Capital, and Gavin Baker, managing partner and chief investment officer of Atreides Management, have sent a joint letter to $NVDA board.

They ask the board to pursue "a slow, measured, and deliberate process regarding the future leadership of Nvidia that leaves all options on the table, including the potential return of Jensen Huang."

"There are more questions about recent events than answers," they write, warning the board to "avoid a rush to replace Jensen that undermines and thwarts the best interests of shareholders." They say the company will be "capably led in the interim by Colette Kress and team" and that the board has time to get the decision right.

A petition site has also launched demanding the board reinstate Huang pending an independent investigation, under the line "thirty-three years deserve an answer."

Elon Musk has joined the calls for Huang's reinstatement, according to the Washington Post.

The board said earlier today it has not formally engaged any candidates and has not yet selected a search firm.
